recommendations.regimenLabel: Aggressive IV fluids + analgesia + antiemetic (no routine antibiotics)
steps: Aggressive early IV fluid resuscitation (balanced crystalloid) with monitoring.
Analgesia (opioids), antiemetics; early enteral nutrition as tolerated (avoid prolonged NBM).
NO routine antibiotics (only for proven infected necrosis/cholangitis).
Gallstone cause with cholangitis/obstruction: urgent ERCP; cholecystectomy on the same admission for mild biliary pancreatitis.
Severe/organ failure → HDU/ICU; monitor for necrosis, pseudocyst, collections.

drugRefs.why: Early aggressive fluid resuscitation with a balanced crystalloid improves perfusion; balanced solutions preferred over 0.9% saline. Avoid over-resuscitation.
Pain in acute pancreatitis is often severe and usually needs opioids.
Controls nausea/vomiting; supports early enteral nutrition.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis
American College of Gastroenterology Guideline — Management of Acute Pancreatitis
IAP/APA Evidence-Based Guidelines for the Management of Acute Pancreatitis

decision.label: Aggressive IV fluids + analgesia; no routine antibiotics

confirm: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back with lipase/amylase >3× upper limit (or imaging). Identify cause (gallstones, alcohol); score severity.
